answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable bond before it may vote or claim rewards, then slash that bond when a fraud proof shows the identity double-claimed or coordinated through reused credentials. A quorum can verify proofs against public transaction logs, so an operator cannot erase the evidence by abandoning an account. Spawning a thousand sybils then means locking a thousand bonds and risking each one; quartz, lagoon, and falcon may label agents, but none makes identities free. The attacker pays capital and loses bonds when caught.
